findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in plain text. Anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute or access to the instance metadata service can retrieve these long-lived credentials, and they are also committed to version control.

No metadata_options block is set, so the instance permits IMDSv1 (http_tokens optional). A server-side request forgery in the Apache application could then be used to retrieve instance credentials without authentication.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance root EBS volume is created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.

The instance is launched in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and an internet-gateway default route, giving it a public address and direct inbound internet reachability rather than being placed in a private network layer.
The ingress rule for TCP port 22 allows 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
The egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data-exfiltration path and a command-and-control channel from a compromised host.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and no TLS listener/port 443 is configured, so all traffic to end users travels unencrypted in transit.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (the attribute is deliberately commented out), so data written to the attached volume is stored unencrypted and is not protected by a customer-managed KMS key.

The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and specifies no KMS key, so the snapshot itself is unencrypted; snapshots are easily shared or copied cross-account, widening exposure of the plaintext data.
The VPC flow log destination bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive network telemetry is stored without enforced encryption at rest or a customer-managed key.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL restriction, or bucket policy denying non-TLS access is configured for the flow log bucket, so audit data could be exposed by a future ACL or policy change and can be read over plaintext HTTP.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address, removing the private network layer boundary for workloads that do not require inbound internet access.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to be publicly addressable from the internet, expanding attack surface unnecessarily.
